result:
Verdict: ACCEPT WITH LIMITATIONS.

I found no material blocker in the frozen candidate at bf3fb50 against base 850d785. The semantics are internally consistent, every generic obligation has a nonvacuous statement reachable from existing lemmas, the financial fixtures are feasible with the existing exact-rational kernel, and thirteen of the fourteen mutation targets have an obvious production site with a discriminating runtime oracle. The corrections below are ranked by how likely they are to cost a revision cycle during implementation. None changes the design's semantics, and the fail-closed runner would catch each of them rather than produce a false pass, which is why they are limits rather than blockers.

First, design.md section 6, mutation 12 (drop a successful peer receipt from accounting aggregation). The accounting result is described in section 3 as a proof, and the runner strips Interleaving proof tails, so a mutant that only edits a definition consumed by theorems compiles and survives. The smallest correction is one sentence in section 6 family 6 requiring an executable supply-aggregation function over the global attempt log, defined before the proof marker, with a named runtime comparison against an independently expected per-domain/asset number on a fixture where both branches change supply. This mirrors the Sprint 6 both-receipts oracle and is the only way the designated oracle can flip.

Second, design.md section 2 and section 6, mutations 10 and 11 (global-position boundary lookup, wrong branch-local invocation selection). The design keeps two counters per branch, consumed slots and successful index, and they coincide for every attempted step because a branch halts on its first refusal. A mutant that swaps one counter for the other is therefore a no-op survivor. Add one sentence stating that these two mutants must select by global schedule position or by the peer's counter, never by the coinciding own counter. The same observation is worth recording in section 2 as an explicit lemma target, since it is what makes the Sprint 6 failure index and the shared runner's failure index agree.

Third, design.md section 6, mutation 9 (output snapshot recomputation). Freezing is implemented by the existing Sprint 5 snapshots function, which stores values without cells, so there is no line in the new namespace whose deletion recomputes anything. The mutant must add code, for example rewriting own history inside advance by looking up each port's cell through the catalog and reading the current shared world. That is feasible and the section 7 helper clause permits it, but the frozen mutation spec should name this site so the mutant is not improvised at task 7.3.

Fourth, design.md section 6, mutation 14 (canonical observation omission of exact failure). If the named projection is a bare call to the existing Parallel observeBranch, the Interleaving module inventory cannot reach the site under the established runner's scoped-module rule. Require the projection to be a definition in the Interleaving namespace that builds the BranchObservation from local branch state, so the mutant edits the function that public recovery checks actually call.

Fifth, design.md section 6 family 2 and mutation 7 (retry halted suffix). A refused single-invocation branch has no later token in a complete schedule, so a retry mutant cannot be exercised. State that the refusing branch in the replenishment fixture has at least one further static slot scheduled after the peer replenishment, and that the expected result records that slot as skipped with an unchanged world.

On the proof plan. The disjoint recovery simulation in section 5 is sound as sketched: shared-world agreement with each isolated cursor on that branch's analyzed read region is preserved by own steps through executeStep_congr and by peer steps through executeStep_target_frame combined with compatibility, using analyzeBranchFrom_member to obtain each slot's footprint at the same local boundary the shared runner uses. The final merge case splits exactly on left writes, right writes, and the framed remainder, with writes contained in reads by analyzeBranchFrom_writes_read. Refusal equality follows from executeStep_refusal_iff and halted branches are handled by the skipped-slot inertia lemma. One wording limit: the specs say the projection "equals" the parallel observation, but the existing comparison is ObservationallyEquivalent, and World carries a proof field. Either state the theorem as ObservationallyEquivalent or note that equality is derived through funext and proof irrelevance; do not let the implementation quietly weaken one into the other.

The interference rule in section 4 is a correct initialized rely/guarantee induction and is not circular: the local obligation is proved without the peer invariant, and the cross-inclusion plus stability premises discharge the peer case. The total-USD10 instance genuinely has overlapping support that Sprint 6's disjoint-region invariant theorem cannot handle, and its local proof reuses the no-supply template lemma. Its limitation is that the local obligation never uses the own-invariant hypothesis, so the instance does not exercise the conditional form of the rule. This is acceptable for the sprint but should be labeled as such in the proof inventory rather than described as a fully exercised instance.

Nonblocking limits beyond the above. The mutation projection will now retain Parallel proofs as well as Composition and Typed proofs, so each of the fifteen compiles is larger than in Sprint 6; the new runner should size its subprocess timeout accordingly rather than inheriting 240 seconds and blocking on time. Mutations 3 and 4 overlap on the competing-liquidity oracle and the design already requires reporting that dependence. Mutation 2's protected siblings are the disjoint fixtures, which should be named explicitly. The execution spec's phrase "cannot make an invalid complete schedule publicly admitted" should read "invalid schedule". Task 1.1 is marked complete; I could not verify strict OpenSpec validation and treat it as claimed. Trust in catalog, registry, authenticated boundaries, observation truth and the fixed initial capability store remains explicit and outside the proofs, revocation races are out of scope by design, review is advisory, all fixtures are development cases, and the six-schedule enumeration is regression evidence subordinate to the universal theorem, as the candidate itself states.

Scope reviewed. I read the full OpenSpec proposal, design, four specs and tasks; the wiki index and Sprint 7 decision page; the roadmap; the planning coverage map and source-context manifest; AGENTS.md and the approved migration design; the Lean toolchain, lakefile and manifest; AxiomAudit; the five Typed modules; the five Composition modules; the seven Parallel modules; the two Parallel mutation scripts; and the Sprint 6 mutation spec. I did not see Typed Examples, the Parallel Audit or Verify drivers, the kernel import root, or any Sprint 6 evidence records, so counts and pass claims cited from the roadmap are taken as stated. No Sprint 7 code exists and none was evaluated; this is a planning verdict only.
